questions.question: Your work at Billings Public Schools includes data audits, reporting, relational databases, and spreadsheet tracking. Which database platforms and query languages have you used hands-on, and can you walk through a data-quality issue you diagnosed and resolved?

This role requires extensive hands-on Scala and Apache Spark experience. What exposure, if any, have you had to Scala, Spark, or other distributed data-processing tools, and how have you built your capability in these areas?

Describe a time when you translated data requirements for an application to staff or customers at Billings Public Schools. How did you clarify the requirement, document it, and verify that the resulting data or report met their needs?

Suppose a new ETL pipeline begins producing duplicate or incomplete student-record data shortly before a reporting deadline. How would you investigate the issue, protect data integrity, communicate with stakeholders, and validate the fix?

The position calls for Java, Spring, and REST API development. Please describe any software-development, programming, API, or automation work you have completed; if you have not yet worked with these technologies, how would you approach closing that gap?

You established administrative procedures to reduce errors and avoidable delays in your current role. What specific process did you change, what evidence showed it was an improvement, and how did you gain adoption from the people using it?

Data engineers here design and deploy databases, ETL pipelines, features, and systems rather than primarily maintaining data records. What interests you about making that transition from education data operations into a software-focused data engineering role?

How would you design a reliable process to ingest data from several school systems into a relational database, including source validation, transformation rules, error handling, auditability, and access controls for confidential records?

Tell us about a situation in which you had to coordinate among stakeholders with different priorities—for example staff, union representatives, programmers, or engineers—to resolve a data or operational issue. What was your role and outcome?

This role works in a collaborative, self-directed engineering environment and values cloud experience, particularly AWS. What experience or learning have you had with cloud technologies, the software development lifecycle, or working with technical delivery teams, and how do you stay motivated when learning unfamiliar tools?
